$$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_n=V,\qquad \dim V_j=j.$$

$$\operatorname{span}(e_0,\ldots,e_{k-1})=\operatorname{span}(v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}).$$

$$u_k=v_k-\sum_{j<k}\langle v_k,e_j\rangle e_j,\qquad e_k=\frac{u_k}{\lVert u_k\rVert}.$$

$$P^2=P\qquad\text{and}\qquad P^*=P.$$

In that case it is the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}P$, along $\ker P=(\operatorname{im}P)^\perp$. The cases $P=0$ and $P=I$ are included.

In the primary decomposition $V=\bigoplus_{i<r}V_i$ associated with $\mu_T=\prod_{i<r}f_i$, the projection $E_i:V\to V_i$ along the other primary components is a polynomial in $T$. More precisely, if $g_i=\mu_T/f_i$ and $a_if_i+b_ig_i=1$, then

$$E_i=b_i(T)g_i(T).$$
